clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991, within months: you hurt your wrist and stopped playing, you and Rafe fought and he moved out, you were on your own getting high and fixing radios, then by early 1992 you were lost and low with no footing. Your mother filled in your college forms and you let it happen. Each shift piled on the last as your grandfather died, your mother was about to remarry, and you had nowhere to stand.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer and death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within months: you ran out of steam for performing, you had a disastrous audition and were done with it, you were on poor terms with family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour. You met Marisol that winter, moved with her to Fenwick by summer, then split up within the year. Once you were back in Thornbury you sank into deep depression. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home; you dropped in briefly on her sickroom hung over on the way to the airport, and she died in February 2004. The trouble that opened when her cancer was found kept moving through the family over those years.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and your move to Marlow Sound, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you were too drained for conversation with your mother; she pressed you to visit you at Alder Creek and you kept the door shut on her; you told her the timing was wrong and she drove out regardless. Once you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in September, you stopped speaking to her altogether. A year of cutoff followed. No one else's shifts show in those months—every shift is between you and your mother, or your own, in the months around your grandmother's death and your move away.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and her family's closeness, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage in March 2017, within months and into the next two years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along. By October 2019 Wren was swamped—one thing after another, a street party, a fundraising dinner, the drive to the lake for her mother's retirement. You were too strict laying out a plan to settle her; she talks with her father and brother all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear. At the lake weekend you woke from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose. You feel you don't belong. Her anxiety rises when you've had no sleep at family occasions, and the drives home afterward are long and quiet. Each person's shift touches the next: her swamping and your overfunctioning, her fusion with her family and your distance from it, your sleeplessness and her worry, all of it piling up around the closeness of her family and your place in it.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
